summary: Assistance requested: safe deactivation of optimizer stack after perf regression following quant-profile update
description: Issue summary: Customer deployed a new quantization profile + aggressive batching and prefix-cache settings yesterday evening. Within ~2 hours they observed intermittent 5xx/503 responses and a sustained tail-latency increase for long-chat sessions. Impact: Several paying users experienced timeouts; customer reports spike in errors ~1.6% of requests resulting in degraded UX. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-west, reserved GPUs (A10G), serving-runtime v2.14.2, optimizer-agent v1.7. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send multi-turn chat with 8+ message history and variable prompt lengths (~2-4k tokens). 2) Target model redwood-3.2 with quant_profile=aggressive-8bit and batching.max_batch_size=128. 3) Observe at steady state under 50 rps. Observed behavior: increased 503 and occasional OOM warnings in node logs, 95th/99th latency moved from 240ms/420ms to 1.2s/2.8s respectively. Expected behavior: minor latency improvements and token-cost reduction without service degradation. Additional context: Customer applied quant profile and optimizer suggestions from Optimize tool earlier today and rolled out to all dedicated nodes with a single config push. They followed the console recommendation but did not run a canary for long-chat workloads. Temporary workaround attempted by customer: reduced batch size to 32 which reduced error rates but did not fully restore tail latency. Request: Step-by-step safe deactivation plan for optimizer stack (quant profile, batching, KV/prefix cache), verification checks to validate rollback, and minimal-impact sequencing so customer can restore stable service without full cluster redeploy.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Elena Morales (Support): Opening ticket after on-call escalation from HorizonHealth. Attached sample logs and token traces. Asking for prioritized guidance; customer is P1 and on Dedicated plan.

2026-03-10 - Kai Nguyen (SRE): Acknowledged. Requesting exact config snapshot and admin CLI access window. Suggested we schedule a 30-min troubleshooting window with HorizonHealth tomorrow morning PST.

2026-03-11 - HorizonHealth (Customer): Provided config bundle (anonymized) and link to internal perf grafana: https://grafana.horizon.example/d/redwood/latency. Confirmed canary was skipped due to time pressure.

2026-03-11 - Kai Nguyen (SRE): Initial hypotheses posted in ticket: (1) quant profile induced slower kernel fallbacks for long sequences; (2) aggressive batching increased KV cache pressure causing cache thrash. Requested heap and GPU mem metrics for affected pods.
2026-03-12 - Support (Elena): Noted that reducing batch size to 32 decreased 5xx but tail-latency still elevated. Asked Eng to provide rollback playbook.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Quantization path created kernel mismatch on sequence-splitting code path causing additional memcpy and re-compilations under long contexts. Evidence: spike in kernel-compile logs around 20:13 UTC matching error window.

Hypothesis 2: KV/prefix cache eviction rate increased after batch sizes rose; cache miss ratio jumped from 2% to 18% for long-chat keys. Evidence: cache-miss-rate graph and redis eviction logs linked in customer grafana.

Quick checks run: validated model binary checksum, confirmed no model-version switch. Verified serving-runtime v2.14.2 has known perf-regression for quant_profile aggressive-8bit on long-context paths (internal note RUNTIME-412).

Relevant logs: tail of serving node (redwood-srv-07): 
  E 2026-03-10T20:12:59Z inference:kv_cache.go:142 eviction(steam) rate=0.18
  W 2026-03-10T20:13:02Z runtime:kernel_manager.go:219 compile_fallback triggered for op:matmul_seq_chunk size=2048
  E 2026-03-10T20:13:05Z http:handler.go:88 response=503 upstream_err=oom
Dashboards: customer provided latency and error dashboards; internal perf benchmark run shows similar tail increase with aggressive-8bit and batch>=64 for long sequences.
resolution: Workaround & rollback plan executed as of 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Stepwise plan we provided and executed with customer: 1) Canary the rollback on 10% of nodes: reverted quant_profile from aggressive-8bit -> conservative-8bit and set batching.max_batch_size=48 (command: redwoodctl config apply --cluster horizon-dedicated --patch 'quant_profile=conservative-8bit,batching.max_batch_size=48' --selector nodepool=cpu-optimized --dry-run=false). 2) Disable optimizer-agent speculative fusion: admin toggle 'optimizer.speculative_fusion=false' via console for canary nodes. 3) Monitor KPIs for 30 minutes (5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, KV cache miss). 4) If stable, progressively roll to additional 30% then 100% with 20-min observation windows. 5) Post-rollback: run heap/gpu-mem tooling and collect kernel-compile traces for Eng team. Outcome: After canary, 5xx reduced to baseline and p99 returned to ~420ms. Follow-ups: Eng to open RUNTIME-412 fix (scheduled) and Optimize team to add long-context canary recommendation to console guidance.
follow_up_items: ENG: RUNTIME-412 tracked for kernel-selection fix (owner: @kai).
DX: Update Optimize console recommendations to require long-chat canary for quant profiles impacting >1024 tokens.
SRE: Add automated health-check that flags sudden cache-miss increases when batching changes are applied.
Customer ops: Run nightly small-canary job for the next 3 days and share results in #support-horizonhealth.
